chunks: And from him (Al-Hakam) from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ziyad al-Wasiti who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a group who closed the door on a pigeon from the pigeons of the Sanctuary (Mecca), and he said: 'Upon them is the value of every bird, one dirham, which they use to buy fodder for the pigeons of the Sanctuary.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever drives away the pigeons of the Sanctuary, upon him is the blood-money of a sheep; and if they do not return, upon him is for every bird the blood-money of a sheep.

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh mentioned this in his Risalah, and I did not find it as a narrated hadith. The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever points out game to a person who is in Ihram, and they kill it, upon him is its ransom.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for closing the door on the pigeons of the Haram or pointing out game to a pilgrim in Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling on disrupting the Haram's pigeons, noting that while the chain of transmission for the specific sheep's blood-money penalty is not fully authenticated (mu'snad), the principle is preserved in Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh's Risalah. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between fully authenticated hadiths and accepted juristic opinions regarding financial compensation (diyah) for minor infractions during Hajj.
